summary: Dedicated: p95/p99 latency spikes during peak hours (suspected capacity saturation / noisy-neighbor symptoms) - us-east
description:
Customer reports recurring latency spikes on Dedicated capacity during peak business hours.

Issue Summary
- Symptom: p95/p99 end-to-end latency increases 3–6x for ~30–90 minute windows; p50 mostly stable.
- Impact: customer-facing chat UX degraded; occasional client-side timeouts (no major increase in Redwood 5xx).
- Frequency: daily recurrence, most often 16:30–19:00 UTC.
- Scope: Dedicated pool in us-east; both chat + embeddings traffic affected but more pronounced on long-context chat requests.

Customer-Provided Observations
- Load pattern aligns with their own peak.
- They recently increased max output tokens and enabled streaming for more routes.
- They see request latency spikes even when their app-side concurrency is unchanged.

Environment / Deployment
- Deployment type: Redwood Dedicated
- Region: us-east
- Customer routing: pinned to Dedicated pool (no explicit region failover configured)
- Models impacted: llama-3.1-70b-instruct, qwen2.5-72b-instruct

Triage Checklist (Support)
- [x] Confirm Dedicated vs Hosted routing (confirmed Dedicated pool ID: ded-us-east-17)
- [x] Confirm timeframe windows + sample request IDs (captured below)
- [x] Check for correlated 5xx/429 spike (none; mild increase in client timeouts)
- [x] Check queueing time vs model compute time (queueing increased during spikes)

Request IDs / Examples (customer provided)
- 01HRYQ9K8WZ8K5S9G0J4A7E3N2
- 01HRYQ9M2X7N3V9Y1C6J2S0T4B
- 01HRYQ9P4G3A9M2D7N8Q1R6H5K

Initial Hypotheses
1) Capacity saturation: Dedicated autoscaler not scaling fast enough (insufficient headroom / min replicas too low).
2) Scheduler behavior under long-context traffic: queue depth increases due to prefill-dominant mix; batching increases queueing.
3) Noisy-neighbor-like behavior inside the pool: GPU fragmentation / uneven load across replicas after scale events.

Dashboards / Links (internal)
- Dedicated pool overview (ded-us-east-17): https://dd.internal.redwood.ai/d/dedicated-pool-overview?pool=ded-us-east-17
- Queue time + scheduler depth: https://dd.internal.redwood.ai/d/scheduler-queue?pool=ded-us-east-17
- GPU utilization by replica: https://dd.internal.redwood.ai/d/gpu-utilization?pool=ded-us-east-17
- Token throughput + prefill vs decode time: https://dd.internal.redwood.ai/d/serving-runtime-latency-breakdown?pool=ded-us-east-17

Requested Actions
- Engage SRE to validate capacity saturation vs infrastructure contention and recommend immediate mitigations.
- Provide customer with safe knobs (timeouts/retries, concurrency guidance, optional burst capacity) while investigating.
- Follow-up: Dedicated sizing review + confirm recommended steady-state + burst settings for their peak profile.

Customer Communication Notes
- Customer requested an interim mitigation they can apply today.
- They prefer not to change models or output length unless necessary; open to scaling capacity if needed.

- Autoscaler events occurred but scale-up lagged by ~12–15 minutes; new replicas came up unevenly loaded (one replica >95% while others ~70%).

Hypothesis: pool is running too close to the knee; long-context traffic causes prefill bursts that saturate the pool; autoscaler thresholds are too conservative and min replicas too low for their peak.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Raise min replicas to maintain headroom during expected peak.
2) Increase scale-up aggressiveness (lower target utilization / shorter stabilization window).
3) Temporarily enable burst capacity in the same region (if available).

- Reduce scale-up stabilization window: 10m -> 2m
- Enable burst up to +6 replicas (subject to capacity) for 16:00–20:00 UTC window

Rationale: Their p99 spikes align with queue wait time spikes; compute per token stable. Headroom should keep queue wait time low. The burst cap prevents runaway scaling.

- Mitigation applied: increased min replicas + more aggressive scale-up policy + burst headroom; rebalanced replicas.
- Prevent recurrence: sizing review scheduled; SRE tracking runbook + alert tuning under ENG-2845.
